lines.text: People will drive like it's their first snow. Every year, it's their first snow.
The first flake gets a photo. The thousandth gets a complaint.
Every snowflake is unique, apparently. Nobody's checked.
TV reporters will stand in it and point at it. I cover snow from indoors, like a professional.
Snow means thrilled dogs and very unthrilled people holding the leashes.
The salt trucks finally get to feel important.
Snow makes everything outside quieter. Except the complaining.
Snow makes kids get up early with no alarm. Science has no explanation.
Snow: the one time talking about the weather counts as news.
Snow, and nobody even had to shake me. Take that, snow globes.
Somewhere a school superintendent is about to be loved or hated. No in between.
Snow is the sky's factory reset.
Every coffee out there is a hand warmer first and a drink second.
Car heaters will warm up right as everyone arrives.
The outdoor cats are suddenly very interested in being indoor cats.
Today 'I'll just run out quickly' will be said a lot and believed by nobody.
Every office thermostat is about to become a battleground.
The cold stays put. It's almost as reliable as me.
Every store door will have someone standing just inside it, thawing.
Today's weather has all the warmth of an automated phone line.
Warm places today: inside, inside, and inside. I've been to all three.
The day is generous at first. Then it remembers what month it is.
Every 'I'll be fine' said at first gets a second opinion later.
Later the ice cream trucks will be playing their song to nobody.
The chilly part comes later. Like the bill.
It cools off later. Suddenly the ice in everyone's drink seems excessive.
Later every outdoor seat goes from 'lucky' to 'brave.'
Later every excuse to stay in gets more convincing.
The warm part is short. The cold part has nowhere else to be.
Later the day hits undo on the warm part.
It warms up just long enough for someone to say 'see, it's nice out.'
Today runs like a hotel shower: cold, then perfect, then cold again.
Halfway through, the weather gets generous. Then it checks its bank account.
The warm part in the middle is too short to enjoy and too long to ignore.
The cold steps out for a smoke, then comes right back.
Today's temperature rises and falls like a soufflé. Same disappointment.
The cold is the main show today. The warm part is the commercial break.
The warmth drops by for a bit and doesn't even take its coat off.
Layer off, layer on. Today the weather is doing the hokey pokey.
Later the day gets better without a single software update. Show-off.
The cold is just the opening act. Nobody came to see it.
Later the iced coffee crowd finally gets to look smart.
The cold goes first today. Even the weather likes to get the worst over with.
The weather improves later. It's the only thing today that will.
Today loads like an old web page. The good part shows up last.
The five-dollar umbrellas by the register are back. Built to survive one rain.
Every fresh blowout in town is about to be a waste of money.
The runners will run in it anyway. Then they'll tell everyone.
Rain at some point. Suddenly I'm everyone's favorite screen.
Rain means a sidewalk full of umbrellas, all of them at eye level.
Every windshield wiper in town will be set one speed wrong.
Every parked bike in town is about to get a plastic bag for a hat.
Rain at some point. The yellow 'wet floor' signs finally get their big day.
Water will fall from the sky. Film at eleven.
Later it warms up, and you'll act like you arranged it.
The day gets better later. No pressure to join it.
Later it warms up. You'll need a new thing to complain about. You'll manage.
Later the layer comes off. It deserves a break from holding you together.
Later you'll stretch in the warmth like a cat. A much less elegant cat.
Later the day gets nice. Way out of your league.
You'll call it perfect weather and do nothing with it.
Later you'll feel great. Don't worry, it won't show.
Later you lose a layer and look like a phone without its case: smaller, and a bit sad.
You'll hold the umbrella like you're the main character. You're an extra.
Think of the rain as a rinse. You were overdue.
You'll say you love the rain. You love saying it.
Hood up, you look like a monk who lost a bet.
If the rain ruins your look, I'll need proof there was one.
Your umbrella gets out more than you do.
